title: Closure toolkit: SRE + Legal seller scripts and evaluation evidence
author: Maya Chen
body:
Overview:

This playbook is a compact, seller-facing kit for closing technically complex deals where SRE and legal must sign off. It bundles: a prioritized evidence checklist, persona-specific messaging and scripts, an executable pilot-to-production orchestration, pricing guardrails for commercial negotiation, and a short Security FAQ tailored for prospect CISO/compliance reviewers. Use this document when the prospect requires parallel engineering and legal evaluation (typical for regulated enterprises and platform teams).

Goals:
- Reduce time-to-decision for SRE/legal review from weeks to days.
- Surface deterministic technical evidence that aligns with internal security/compliance gates.
- Give sellers repeatable scripts for addressing common objections.

What this pack contains (one-page view):
1) Executive one-liner and elevator script (for AE).
2) Persona playbooks: SRE, Platform Eng, CISO/Legal, Procurement.
3) Evidence checklist (recommended artifacts to attach to RFPs).
4) Pilot orchestration steps (30/60/90 day pathways) with SLOs and escalation points.
5) Pricing guardrails and simple costing model for pilot-to-scale.
6) Compact Security FAQ with links to deeper evidence.
7) Attachments: sample deck outline, sample SOC/attestation snippets, sample contractual language (data residency, indemnities).

Executive one-liner (AE script):
"Redwood gives you a single inference runtime across hosted, dedicated, and private deployments so your platform team can standardize latency and cost controls while keeping compliance boundaries intact. We'll run a focused 30-day pilot with engineering evidence and legal exhibits up front so you can evaluate risk without build-time investment."

Persona playbooks (short scripts):
- SRE / Platform Engineer:
  - Key concern: predictable latency and tail behavior under burst.
  - Owner script: "We will run the pilot on redwood-dedicated with a 2-node GPU pool configured with the same request mix you expect at scale. We can instrument 95/99 token latency, auto-batching behavior, and KV cache hit-rate; we'll provide trace-level logs in the console and a sampling of p95/p99 traces for validation."
  - Ask: access to representative traffic sample and a staging OAuth token.

- CISO / Legal:
  - Key concern: data residency, auditability, and contractual protections.
  - Owner script: "Redwood supports VPC private deployments and KMS-backed key management for on-prem or cloud private deployments. For hosted pilots we can enable TLS+mTLS, customer-managed encryption keys, and a restricted audit stream for your legal team to review. We'll provide SOC-type artifacts and an audit-log export for the pilot window."
  - Ask: list of minimum compliance evidence items they require (e.g., SOC2, ISO, DPA clauses).

- Procurement / Finance:
  - Key concern: predictable pilot cost and conversion economics.
  - Owner script: "We will structure a time-boxed pilot with a capped spend and conversion options to Reserved/Dedicated capacity. Your finance team will see a pilot estimate in the pilot pricing worksheet; we include clear, line-item token economics so you can model go/no-go decisions."

Evidence checklist (attach in RFP response or demo follow-up):
- Architecture diagrams: service-level diagram showing redwood-api, redwood-console, redwood-dedicated, and optional redwood-private VPC peering.
- Performance evidence: benchmark run of comparable model variant (model name + quantization profile), sample p50/p95/p99 token latency and throughput numbers for the prospect's median request length.
- Observability artifacts: example per-route dashboards, a 7-day token breakdown CSV, and a tracing sample (jaeger/span export).
- Security & compliance: SOC2 summary, encryption-at-rest description, KMS integration notes, sample audit log export (anonymized).
- Data handling: DPA excerpt showing data residency language and retention windows.
- Contract samples: sample SOW with pilot scope, SLA excerpt, and example indemnity/data covenant language.
- Integration docs: sample SDK snippet, API keys rotation steps, and SSO/OAuth config doc.

Pilot orchestration (recommended 30/60/90 cadence):
- Phase 0 — Kickoff (Day 0–3):
  1) Align objectives: measurable acceptance criteria (functional, SLOs, security gates).
  2) Share artifacts: prospect provides representative traffic profile and security checklist.
  3) Activate pilot environment: create redwood-dedicated pool or redwood-private sandbox.
  Ownership: Solutions Engineer (SE) + AE.

- Phase 1 — Engineering validation (Day 4–30):
  1) Baseline test: run 2 full-load scenarios (typical and peak) using the provided profile.
  2) Capture metrics: token p50/p95/p99 latency, error rate, cost-per-token, KV cache hit-rate, batching efficiency.
  3) Provide artifacts: dashboard link, CSV exports, sample traces, and an annotated runbook of any tuning performed.
  Acceptance criteria examples:
  - Latency: p95 token latency < 300 ms for typical profile, p99 below 800 ms for peak bursts (adjust per prospect tolerances).
  - Reliability: 99.9% successful token generation (errors < 0.1%).
  - Cost signals: measured per-1M-token cost for the chosen model variant and quantization.
  Ownership: SE + SRE contact (Redwood).

- Phase 2 — Compliance review (Day 10–45, parallel):
  1) Deliver compliance artifacts: SOC2 summary, audit log samples, contract excerpts (DPA), encryption & key management details.
  2) Address legal redlines: provide clause-by-clause explanations and reference customers (anonymized use-cases).
  Ownership: Legal + Security Solutions Engineer.

- Phase 3 — Business validation & handoff (Day 30–90):
  1) Run customer acceptance tests with traffic in staging or shadow mode.
  2) Show observability during live-run and demonstrate rollback/fallback to a cheaper model variant or regional fallback.
  3) Negotiate long-term commercial terms (reserved capacity, enterprise support).
  Ownership: AE + Customer Success + Product Ops.

Rollout controls and safe-fallbacks (technical):
- Canary rollout pattern: start at 1% production traffic -> 10% -> 50% -> 100% with health gates at each step.
- Health gates (must pass to advance): token error rate < 0.2% for 10m windows; latency p95 within accepted delta vs baseline; no new regression alerts from Redwood Optimize.
- Fallbacks: automatic reroute to commodity model variant (lower-cost/CPU variant) or to regionally compliant fallback endpoint.

Pricing guardrails and example pricing worksheet:
- Pilot pricing model: time-boxed flat fee + capped usage (token cap + overage rate).
- Conversion guidance: typical conversion path is pilot -> 6–12 month reserved commitment sized at 2–5x pilot peak throughput.
- Example calculation (simple):
  - Pilot flat fee: $12,000 (30 days) + included 10M tokens.
  - Overage: $0.80 per 1k tokens beyond cap.
  - Estimated 1M tokens/day at pilot peak -> pilot cost = $12,000 + (20M extra tokens * $0.0008) = $12,000 + $16,000 = $28,000.
  - If converting to Dedicated: typical discount 30–45% off hosted list in exchange for 12-month commit.

Competitive positioning (short brief):
- Differentiator 1: unified runtime across hosted/dedicated/private with identical API surface (reduces migration/ops friction).
- Differentiator 2: model-aware serving optimizations (auto-batching, KV caching, quantization profiles) that reduce unit cost without manual kernel tuning.
- Common competitor objections and suggested responses:
  - "We can self-host cheaper." -> "Self-host cost can be lower at scale but requires bespoke ops and lacks our rollout controls, model variants, and continuous-eval guardrails — we provide a migration path that preserves your SLAs with less engineering overhead."
  - "We need on-prem only." -> "We offer redwood-private with a private control plane and KMS/HSM options; we will provide an on-prem packaging runbook and a KO checklist for air-gapped installs."

Security FAQ (compact):
- Q: How is customer data isolated for hosted pilots?
  A: Each tenant has logical isolation at the routing and storage layers; pilot artifacts can be delivered from a dedicated tenant ID. For additional isolation we recommend redwood-dedicated or redwood-private.
- Q: Which keys do you manage vs the customer?
  A: By default Redwood manages envelope keys; customers can request KMS integration (customer-managed keys) for hosted pilots or bring-your-own HSM in private deployments.
- Q: Can audit logs be exported for 3rd-party review?
  A: Yes — we provide an anonymized audit log export with timestamps, request/response hashes, and decision traces.
- Q: What are typical retention windows during pilot?
  A: Default 30 days; can be adjusted to match prospect policy with accompanying data processing notes.

Sample attachments & templates to include with any prospect packet (short list):
- 1-page technical deck (outline): Problem, Redwood solution, pilot scope, acceptance criteria, SLOs, pricing, next steps.
- Pilot SOW template (editable): scope, deliverables, timelines, acceptance criteria, pilot cap, conversion options.
- SRE tuning checklist: batching configs, KV cache tuning knobs, model quantization profile used.
- Contract excerpt examples: sample DPA, sample SLA, sample SSO/SCIM provisioning clause.

Owner & escalation matrix (single line contacts):
- AE: Primary commercial owner (AE Name placeholder).
- SE: Technical owner during pilot (SE Name placeholder).
- Redwood SRE escalation: oncall-sre@redwood.ai (for pilot infra issues).
- Security/legal: security-requests@redwood.ai and legal@redwood.ai.

How to use this doc in the field (quick checklist for reps):
1) Pre-call: attach the 1-page deck + evidence checklist to intro email.
2) Kickoff: align on acceptance criteria and sign the pilot SOW with a capped spend.
3) Week 1–2: run baseline tests and deliver first observability artifacts.
4) Week 3–4: parallel compliance artifact delivery and legal Q/A; adjust pilot if needed.
5) Close: convert to reserved or private deployment with negotiated ramp and support SLAs.

Appendix: sample CLI/SDK snippets we typically attach (anonymized):
- API: curl -H 'Authorization: Bearer <TOKEN>' -d '{"model":"example-model","input":"..."}' https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate
- Example config: {
  "deployment":"dedicated-pilot-01",
  "batching": { "max_tokens": 1024, "latency_target_ms": 300 },
  "kv_cache": { "enabled": true, "ttl_seconds": 3600 }
}

Notes and recommended next steps for the rep who uses this kit: attach the completed evidence checklist as a single ZIP to the opportunity record, record the pilot acceptance criteria on the CRM, and request a security intake meeting (20–40 minutes) within the first week of the pilot.

Related pages and deeper evidence: link the related pages list at top of this doc and include pointer to the security evidence folder in Drive when exchanging artifacts.

Change history: initial published 2027-11-05; updated pricing examples and pilot SOW language 2028-02-10.
